helps.text: wise man; wise one, a direct address. This is the weak masculine singular of wīs used substantivally; its local personal use is supplied.
helps.scope_note: Local reading scaffold, unless a separately listed form/sense/construction is explicitly taught.

helps.anchor: ðē is geðūht … wesan / mē is geðūht … healdan
helps.text: To you it seems … to be / to me it seems … to hold. Treat these source expressions as whole supported frames. The person to whom it seems is dative. Cook explicitly labels furðra nominative singular; do not force the whole passage into a newly generalized accusative-and-infinitive rule.
helps.scope_note: Local reading scaffold, unless a separately listed form/sense/construction is explicitly taught.

helps.text: among these (occupations). Betweox and betweoh are the two exact spellings here; the following phrase is accusative plural. In the first question cræftas is understood after ðās.
helps.scope_note: Local reading scaffold, unless a separately listed form/sense/construction is explicitly taught.

helps.text: foremost; prior, weak comparative masculine nominative singular, exactly as Cook’s note14 identifies it. This one form/sense is supplied.
helps.scope_note: Local reading scaffold, unless a separately listed form/sense/construction is explicitly taught.

helps.anchor: swā-swā hit is gerǣd on godspelle
helps.text: just as it is read in the Gospel. Swā-swā means just as; gerǣd is the exact past participle used in this passive expression. This supplied phrase is not a new complete passive system.
helps.scope_note: Local reading scaffold, unless a separately listed form/sense/construction is explicitly taught.

helps.text: First seek (plural command). Sēceað is Cook’s exact source spelling; the selected productive plural command is sēcað. Retain and recognize this attested variant.
helps.scope_note: Local reading scaffold, unless a separately listed form/sense/construction is explicitly taught.

helps.anchor: ðās ðing eall bēoð tōgēiecte ēow
helps.text: all these things will be added to you. Eall agrees with neuter plural ðing. Bēoð is third-person plural here, and ēow is the dative recipient. Tōgēiecte is a source predicate participle: retain its -e under Cook’s explicit predicate-participle rule (§62), rather than changing it to a presumed neuter ending.
helps.scope_note: Local reading scaffold, unless a separately listed form/sense/construction is explicitly taught.

helps.text: worldly occupations (accusative plural) / chief place, primacy (accusative singular). These exact source words are supplied synonyms within the question. Cook prints woruldcræftas but records manuscript cræftas woruld.
helps.scope_note: Local reading scaffold, unless a separately listed form/sense/construction is explicitly taught.

helps.text: feeds us all. Ūs is accusative plural, ealle refers to the people fed (masculine plural), and fēt is present indicative third singular of fēdan. This exact verb form is supplied; the distinct productive āfēdan has its own full system.
helps.scope_note: Local reading scaffold, unless a separately listed form/sense/construction is explicitly taught.

helps.text: Cook marks the is in each Teacher question and in swā-swā hit is gerǣd as conjectural, absent from his manuscripts. Preserve those editorial insertions with their note; the is in mē is geðūht belongs to a separate note15.
helps.scope_note: Local reading scaffold, unless a separately listed form/sense/construction is explicitly taught.

helps.text: God’s service, service of God; his righteousness. The genitives identify the divine possessor or object of service; his can follow its noun in the exact source. The service sense of ðēowdōm is new in this unit.
helps.scope_note: Local reading scaffold, unless a separately listed form/sense/construction is explicitly taught.
